subject: Trading
title: The Asian Financial Crisis: 1997
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Asian Financial Crisis: 1997.

hook.text: Thailand abandoned its currency peg on July 2, 1997. The Asian economic miracle unraveled within months.

buildup.text: Asian tigers—Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, South Korea—had boomed on foreign capital and dollar-pegged currencies.

discovery.text: When Thailand's peg broke, foreign investors fled all Asian markets simultaneously. Currencies and stocks cratered.

twist.text: The IMF provided bailouts but demanded harsh austerity measures, deepening the recession in affected countries.

climax.text: The crisis proved that hot money—foreign capital that flows in easily—can flow out just as easily, devastating all.

punchline.text: Easy money in means easy money out.

quiz.question: What triggered the 1997 Asian Financial Crisis?
options: A stock market crash in Japan
Thailand abandoned its currency peg, triggering regional capital flight
